title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
An established and growing property business in Hull is looking to appoint an Assistant Management Accountant to strengthen its in house finance team. The business has a diverse portfolio of commercial property interests alongside an active pipeline of development and investment activity, providing a varied environment for someone looking to develop their management accounting experience.

Working as part of a small finance team, the Assistant Management Accountant will support the production of timely and accurate management information across the group. This is a broad role combining month end accounting with transactional oversight, balance sheet work and financial analysis. There will be good exposure to different entities and property related projects, making it well suited to someone studying towards a professional accounting qualification.

Responsibilities
- Assist with the preparation of monthly management accounts across a portfolio of companies.
- Prepare and post accruals, prepayments and other month-end journals.
- Complete balance sheet reconciliations and investigate outstanding items.
- Support budgeting, forecasting and cash flow reporting.
- Assist with the analysis of income, expenditure and performance against budget.
- Maintain accurate accounting records across multiple entities and cost centres.
- Support VAT returns and other routine financial reporting requirements.
- Assist with purchase and sales ledger activity where required, ensuring transactions are correctly recorded and allocated.
- Provide financial information and analysis to colleagues across the wider business.
- Support year end processes and provide information for the external accountants and auditors.

Candidate Profile
- AAT qualified or studying towards ACCA, CIMA or ACA, with study support potentially available.
- Previous experience within an accounts or finance team, ideally with some exposure to management accounts.
- Comfortable working with accruals, prepayments, journals and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Good Excel skills and confidence working with accounting systems.
- Able to manage responsibilities across multiple companies, projects or cost centres.
- Good attention to detail with a practical approach to resolving accounting queries.
- Comfortable working in a small finance team where responsibilities can be varied.

Package and Working Pattern
- Salary: £30,000 - £40,000
- Full-time, permanent position.
- Hull based.
- Study support for an appropriate professional accounting qualification can be considered.
- Opportunity to work across a varied group structure and commercial property portfolio.

We have built our business on long term relationships with both individuals and clients in all sectors, bringing real benefits to all concerned. title: Family Support Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Family Support Coordinator

Contract: Fixed-Term for 1 year

Hours: 28 hours per week

Salary: £21,213.98 per annum (£26,517.48 FTE)

Location: Kingston Upon Hull

About Coram

Coram is committed to improving the lives of the UK's most vulnerable children and young people.

We support children and young people from birth to independence, creating a change that lasts a lifetime.

Coram is the UK's oldest children's charity founded by Thomas Coram in London helping vulnerable children and young people since 1739. Today, the Coram group helps more than one million children, young people, families and professionals every year by providing access to the skills and opportunities they need to thrive.

Coram Family Lives is part of the Coram group.

About the role

Are you passionate about helping families thrive and making a genuine difference?

Coram Family Lives is seeking an experienced, enthusiastic and compassionate Family Support Coordinator to provide individual and group support for families with children aged 0-5 in Kingston upon Hull.

You will provide practical and emotional support, helping parents manage the challenges of family life. You will ensure they have the information and tools to care for and interact positively with their children while supporting their own wellbeing.

You will support parents from pregnancy through early parenthood, promote positive parent-infant relationships and perinatal mental health, and help reduce stigma around these topics. You will also build parents' confidence, support children's learning and development at home, and help families experiencing parental conflict.

You will provide one-to-one support and engaging workshops, and help families access community activities and services, including SEND and early years provision. Your work will improve outcomes for children and strengthen family wellbeing.

You will work with Family Hub teams, early years practitioners, health professionals and community partners. You will also develop a network of volunteers to provide informal support across local communities.

Why Join Us?
- A rewarding opportunity to make a lasting difference to families.
- Variety, autonomy and meaningful relationship-based work.
- The chance to develop partnerships across a range of services.
- Be part of a respected national charity with almost 50 years of supporting families.
- If you're a skilled, empathetic professional who is passionate about helping families flourish, we'd love to hear from you.

Join us and help children and families thrive, whatever life brings

The salary for 28 hours per week is £21,213.98per annum.

To apply for this role, please click on the redirect to recruiter button to complete the application.

Closing Date: Sunday, 4th October

Interview Date: TBC

Coram is an equal opportunities employer, and we believe a diverse workforce enables us to improve the services to the children and families we help. We are genuinely committed to encouraging candidates from all sections of the community we seek to support. This includes those from global majority ethnic backgrounds, those that identify as LGBQT+, those with disabilities, those with lived experience of care, those with neurodiversity, and those from other groups who are underrepresented at Coram.

If applicants feel comfortable, we encourage them to draw on lived experience as well as professional experience in their personal statement as part of their application.

We are committed to the safeguarding of children and where appropriate will require the successful applicant to undertake a check from the Disclosure and Barring Service.

title: Interim Assistant Accountant

description:

title: Warranties Administrator - Automotive
description:
Warranties Administrator

Hull Full-Time Permanent£28,000 per annum

Our client, a well-established automotive business based in Hull, is seeking a Warranties Administrator to join their busy aftersales team on a full-time, permanent basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced automotive administration professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced dealership or workshop environment and takes pride in delivering accurate and efficient administrative support.

The Role

As a Warranties Administrator, you will be responsible for accurately costing and invoicing completed workshop jobs across multiple vehicle brands, ensuring all work is processed correctly and in line with manufacturer and company requirements.

Key responsibilities include:
- Costing completed workshop jobs accurately and efficiently
- Processing service and repair invoices
- Administering warranty claims in line with manufacturer guidelines
- Ensuring all documentation is complete and compliant
- Liaising with workshop, service and parts departments to resolve any discrepancies
- Maintaining accurate records and supporting the wider aftersales function
- Ensuring all submissions and invoicing are completed within required timescales

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have previous experience within the automotive industry in one of the following areas:
- Aftersales Administration
- Service Invoicing
- Warranty Administration
- Workshop Costing
- Dealership Administration

You will also possess:
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise workload effectively
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving
- Confidence working with dealership management systems

Experience using Kerridge would be a distinct advantage.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary of £28,000 per annum
- Full-time, permanent position
- Opportunity to join a successful and growing automotive business
- Supportive and professional working environment
- Career development opportunities within the automotive sector

Apply Today

If you have experience in automotive aftersales administration, service invoicing, warranty administration or workshop costing and are looking for your next opportunity in Leeds, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to be considered.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking to employ a part time Receptionist to join our friendly team. The successful candidate will be required to provide effective and efficient reception and administrative services for the practice in a professional and courteous manner. Experienced in delivering a high standard of customer service is valued but full training for this role will be provided. The role is for 16 hours per week to cover maternity leave for 12 months . Also there is a need to be able to cover colleagues for sickness and holiday absence. Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice, including the provision clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Ensure efficient running of appointment system. Be aware of flow of patients into consulting rooms and advise patients regarding any potential delays. Help coordinate urgent on the day appointments for patients either by assisting with the online forms or walk-in emergencies. Respond to all queries and requests for assistance from patients and other visitors. Participate in Care Navigation, which involves signposting patient to more appropriate health care services. Take and process new patient registrations. Safely take samples from patients as per the Sample Handing protocol. Take subject access requests from patients. Set up online user accounts. Ensure that you are familiar with the appointment systems being used for the practice and Primary Care Network appointments. Book appointments for long term condition recalls as per the patients needs. Process patient information such as notifications of deaths as per practice protocols. Receive and transfer telephone calls. Ensure accurate messages are transcribed to the relevant recipient. To assist with the Practices clerical work as required. This may involve clinical data entry onto the computer, scanning of documents, issuing mail-merge letters, recording and extracting data for audit purposes. To retrieve and advise patients of their tests results. To provide holiday and sickness cover for colleagues as required. This list is not exhaustive and other duties relative to the role may apply.
